title: A trader cannot record a microchip number for a dog or a horse anywhere in Frontend; Design release 1 asks for one on both

finding.frontend: Frontend knows six ways to identify an animal and a microchip is not one of them: passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, and — only for commodities that have no specific identifier at all — free-text identification details and a description (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198). The word microchip appears nowhere in src/server outside a test fixture, where it is typed as a value into the free-text field. The gap bites hardest on the two commodities that need it: because dogs and horses do have specific identifiers, the free-text fallback is switched off for them, so a trader importing a dog is shown a passport and a tattoo field and nothing else. The captured DOM of fe-animal-identification bears this out — the dog line offers animalIdentifierPassport-2 and animalIdentifierTattoo-2, the horse line animalIdentifierPassport-1 and horseName-1, and there is nowhere on the page to put a chip number.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 asks for a microchip on both. Its identifiers are declared per commodity code, and a dog (01061900) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Tattoo while a horse (0101) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Horse name (app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:4-17). Microchipping is how a dog is identified in law, so the field is not decoration.
finding.difference: Add a microchip identifier and apply it to the dog and horse commodities. In Frontend that is a seventh obligation beside passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js, an allowlist beside the existing four in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:107-115, a label and an error message in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-72, and its addition to the specific-identifier union so the free-text fallback keeps behaving as it does today. It cannot stop there: the value has to reach the outbox, and the animal identifier record the backend sends to GBNAG recognises only the type codes EAR_TAG and PASSPORT (trade-imports-animals-backend, TradeProductInstance.AnimalIdentifier), so a MICROCHIP type code and the field that feeds it are backend work that has to land alongside.
finding.falsifiedBy: A microchip field rendered on Frontend's animal identification page for a dog or a horse, or a microchip value carried anywhere in Frontend's notification payload. This was read from source on both sides and not photographed: Design release 1's identification capture was taken with cattle selected, whose identifiers are ear tag and passport, so no capture in this corpus shows the field. Capturing dr1-animal-identification-details with commodity 01061900 or 0101 selected would show it.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier on both halves. Case-insensitive grep for microchip across the frontend's whole src tree returns three hits and all three are the string "Microchip 900123" typed as a value into the free-text identification field in two test fixtures, so no microchip field exists. Read capture/html/frontend/fe-animal-identification.html whole and confirmed the dog line at :204-228 offers only animalIdentifierPassport-2 and animalIdentifierTattoo-2 and the horse line at :173-194 only animalIdentifierPassport-1 and horseName-1, with nowhere to put a chip number; opened the 7956-pixel frontend page shot and confirmed the same by eye across all four commodity cards. Read app/data/commodity-identifiers.js whole. Verified the backend claim in the repo rather than taking it on trust: trade-imports-animals-backend TradeProductInstance.java:17-18 declares only EAR_TAG and PASSPORT and :31-36 emits only those two. CORRECT; band needs-backend upheld.
finding.correction: Every leg of the claim checks out, including the backend one, which was verified verbatim rather than accepted. Two records. (1) The control named was the label "Microchip", which appears on neither captured screen — Design release 1's identification capture holds cattle only, and Frontend has no such field by definition — so the crop would have been refused on both sides and both cards would have fallen back to the whole page. The controls are now the dog line's two frontend fields, which crop the exact block where the missing field belongs; the Design release 1 side still falls back, and that is unavoidable until a capture with commodity 01061900 selected exists. (2) The backend paragraph is narrower than the truth in a way that helps whoever picks this up: the outbox drops tattoo, horse name and the free-text identifiers today as well, not only microchip, so the contract work is a general one rather than a single new type code.
